harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/inventory ownership and permissions on node1: created inventorysvc (system user) and inventory-readers (group), set owner:group to inventorysvc:inventory-readers recursively, and set mode 750 on directories / 640 on files. Verified original data preserved via matching sha256 checksums before/after, verified inventorysvc and inventory-readers members can read the data while other users are denied, and confirmed the changes persist across a full node reboot (new boot_id observed, permissions/ownership/checksums identical post-restart).
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory: found root:root ownership, world-readable 755/644 perms, no inventorysvc user or inventory-readers group existed
Captured baseline checksums of data/config.json and data/records.csv
Created group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc (primary group inventorysvc, nologin shell) via sudo groupadd/useradd
Recursively chown'd /srv/inventory to inventorysvc:inventory-readers
Set directories to 750 and files to 640 recursively
Verified content unchanged via sha256sum match before/after
Positively tested access: inventorysvc can read files (rc=0), a test user added to inventory-readers can read files (rc=0, then cleaned up), and user 'nobody' is denied (permission denied, rc=1)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state proof on node1
Issued 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded via nohup so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec became available again, confirming a changed boot_id (151c4aa9... -> f813c49b...), proving an actual reboot occurred
Re-verified post-restart: ownership, permissions, checksums identical to pre-restart, and access control (inventorysvc allowed, nobody denied) still enforced

evidence.requirement: Baseline discovery: existing data owned by root, world-readable, no inventorysvc/inventory-readers present
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/inventory and its files were root:root with 755/644 perms; inventorysvc user did not exist
sha256sum of config.json and records.csv captured before changes and matched sha256sum after chown/chmod, proving content preservation
Created inventorysvc system user, chown -R to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, verified via ls -la showing inventorysvc as owner on all paths
Created inventory-readers group, applied as group owner with 750/640 perms; a test user added to inventory-readers successfully read records.csv (rc=0)
Non-privileged shell user 'antrieb' got Permission denied listing the directory; user 'nobody' (not in inventory-readers) got Permission denied reading records.csv (rc=1)

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart - healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 151c4aa9-9e81-4a32-9c22-08c5c441403a and confirmed /srv/inventory perms/ownership/checksums healthy immediately before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart - acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via nohup; exec call returned 'reboot issued' with exit_code 0 before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart - proof of disconnection and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Subsequent exec timed out (node down mid-reboot); later poll succeeded with new boot_id f813c49b-7e9a-4d7d-a782-c488aa58ecbf, differing from baseline, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart - post-restart recovery of required state
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers), permissions (750/640), and file checksums matched pre-restart baseline exactly; access control re-verified (inventorysvc allowed, nobody denied)
